events.summary:
At 440 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located near Pinetop Country
Club, or 12 miles southeast of Show Low, moving north at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Pinetop Country Club and McNary.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 60 between mile markers 350 and 361. State Route 61 between
mile markers 353 and 357.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Brown Creek Campground.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Areas of fog have expanded across east-central and northeast
Wisconsin early this morning. The fog was locally dense in spots,
with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less, especially along the
southern bay impacting the city of Green Bay.

If you have travel plans early this morning, be on alert for
rapidly changing or poor visibilities as low as 1/4 mile or less
in spots. Plan on extra time to reach your destination and allow
extra room between you and the car in front of you.

Visibilities should begin to improve from west to east through
sunrise as a cold front moves across the area.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Arizona, including the following
area, Northwest Plateau.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to
impact portions of northern Mohave County through Thursday.
Storms will be accompanied by heavy rainfall, and a flash
flooding threat may evolve for areas that experience multiple
rounds of heavy rain.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
